grounding.excerpt: Achieve Final Effluent Limitations 12 months after permit effective date

SECTION B - SCHEDULE OF COMPLIANCE ... 1) The permittee shall achieve compliance with the Cyanide effluent limitations specified for discharges in accordance with the following schedule: ... Achieve Final Effluent Limitations 12 months after permit effective date ... a. ... progress report ... b. ... notice of compliance or noncompliance ... c. ... explanation for this delay and proposed remedial actions.

Footnotes *10 and *11 (TDS phased limits: 497 mg/L through 3 years; 449 mg/L thereafter) and Section B.2 TDS compliance schedule — parallel phased-limit structure for a different parameter, not cyanide.

rationale: The obligation asks whether Section B.1's 12-month activity establishes a transition between different enforceable numeric cyanide limits or only a compliance deadline with unchanged applicable limits during the preceding 12 months. The packet grounds Section B.1's schedule language ('Achieve Final Effluent Limitations 12 months after permit effective date') and sub-items (a)-(c) reporting requirements, but does not include the cyanide effluent limitation numeric values referenced by Section B.1, any elsewhere-in-permit interim/final cyanide limit distinction, the permit effective date, or Federal FY2025 monitoring period alignment. The word 'Final' and the TDS phased-limit footnotes (*10/*11) and Section B.2 schedule are structurally suggestive of phased limits but do not establish what numeric cyanide limits apply before versus after the 12-month date. Neither burden is met: there is no establishing evidence of different enforceable cyanide limits at the transition date, nor establishing evidence that the same limits apply throughout with only a compliance deadline. Per P5, unsupported uncertainty is preferred to unsupported semantic closure.
